b: NASHVILLE — This Thanksgiving, families around the country will gather to enjoy time off, companionship and, of course, turkey. This delicious family tradition and food coma are brought to us by the members of the National Turkey Federation (NTF) — an organization that represents the interests of 95% of the U.S. turkey industry.

From turkey growers to processors to breeders to distributors, the entire supply chain relies on the NTF to advocate on their behalf on Capitol Hill, provide crisis management and communications support, and share the information they need to operate their businesses.
There’s another benefit members can be thankful for: the opportunity to participate in the White House Presentation, where two of their fine, feathered friends get pardoned by the President.

On Feb. 17-20, 2027, the NTF’s annual convention will head to Nashville.

“Our membership gets to have the honor and privilege of unofficially kicking off the holiday season,” Leslee Oden, President and CEO of the NTF, said. “It’s really a time-honored, fun tradition that our organization has been a part of, and this year will represent our 79th time at the White House. It’s a great opportunity to put turkey farmers and processors on the global stage.”

On Feb. 17-20, 2027, at the Renaissance Nashville Hotel, the issues of NTF members will take center stage at the organization’s annual convention. During the members-only event, more than 600 attendees will gobble up knowledge that helps them deliver the Thanksgiving dinners we know and love.
“We’re a small but mighty industry and we come together to work for the greater good of the entire industry,” Oden said.

To do this, attendees listen to expert speakers and have discussions during various committee meetings. The conference content focuses on what matters most to members, such as legislative and regulatory issues, animal care strategies and food safety concerns.

“What guides us is simple: We follow the science, we put animal care and food safety first, and we’re led by our members — the growers and processors and allied folks who do the work every day,” Oden said. “We help our members deliver safe and wholesome, high-quality, nutritious turkey to consumers worldwide.”
Just as Americans do during Thanksgiving, NTF members also use the convention as an opportunity to connect with one another as a family of colleagues who share the same challenges and concerns.

“We’re a very small industry as a whole, and I commonly say that the industry is more like a family. Our convention can really act as a family reunion,” Oden added. “Our folks will only see each other once that year, so it’s really meaningful. Members have been fostering relationships around the industry, and they can come together in one place to be brought new information and discuss continuous issues we’ve been battling for many years.”
